Date: 2026-05-25 10:02 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial RFP & high-level ask: reserved capacity options

Sam —

Appreciate the RFP. Quick summary below; I attached a spreadsheet with three sketched packages (A/B/C) and the projected token burn and monthly burn-rate assumptions. High level options: 

Option A — Conservative (Pilot)- Minimum reserved: 6 GPUs (mixed A100/80GB equiv)- Ramp: 6 -> 12 GPUs over 8 weeks (activation trigger: sustained 70% utilization for 2 weeks)- Burst: up to +50% capacity via spot lanes; burst credits applied per-token after baseline consumption- Onboarding: 40k token credit + 2 prewarm windows

Option B — Production (Recommended)- Minimum reserved: 12 GPUs- Ramp: 12 -> 24 GPUs over 12 weeks with staged activation (6 week review)- Burst: dedicated burst pool + fallback to quantized family if spot unavailable- Warm-start: KV cache migration and prefix caching for hot endpoints

Option C — Anchored SLA (Predictable)- Minimum reserved: 24 GPUs + hot-standby for 2 GPUs- Ramp: immediate tranche activation over 4 weeks- Pricing: stepped discount at 6/12/24 month milestones

Notes / assumptions:
- Pricing in the spreadsheet is indicative (see sheet 'pricing_assumptions').
- We recommend Option B for the mix of predictability and cost-efficiency given your qps profile.

Attachments: [Attachment: reserve_options_MarineCore_v1.xlsx (xlsx)]

Next steps: can we schedule a 30-min procurement review Thu or Fri to align on the preferred option + doc signature window?

Regards,
Ben
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-28 15:20 -07:00
Subject: Internal: MarineCore proposal tweaks (warmstart / phased ramp)

Ben / Karthik —

A couple of internal suggested edits before we send an official proposal to Sam:

1) Warmstart credits: add a 2-week 'warm window' that preserves KV cache + prefix caching for top-10 endpoints (helps reduce transient p50 by ~30%).
2) Staged ramp detail: instead of a straight 12->24 over 12 weeks, propose a 3-tranche: 12 (wk0), +6 (wk6), +6 (wk12) with an evaluation checkpoint at each tranche — gives procurement predictable delivery milestones.
3) Fallback policy: list an explicit fallback to a 4-bit quantized variant (same API surface) when demand exceeds reserved + burst for > 30 minutes; quantify expected quality delta and put a rollback path.

If we can include that language in the v2 PDF and call out a standard exception for 'data residency onboarding' (since they mentioned EU customers possibility), we should be good. Also cc Grace O'Connor for onboarding SLA and runbook alignment in the next round.

Marissa
Sr. Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Hi Sam / JP —

Thanks — attached is the updated reserved proposal (v3) that incorporates the warmstart window, the 3-tranche ramp, and an explicit fallback/rollback policy for quantized variants. Key highlights:

- Baseline: 12 reserved GPUs (Option B base) with a staged activation to 24 GPUs in two tranches (wk6, wk12).
- Warmstart: 2-week persistent warm-window for top-10 endpoints; KV cache migration included as onboarding task.
- Burst: Dedicated burst pool with clear consumption rules; we show an example monthly burn and how burst credits are applied.
- SLA: 99.9% availability on reserved lane; 99.5% overall availability with burst/fallback in place.

Action items for MarineCore:
- Confirm preferred option (A/B/C) and which tranche cadence you want for first 6 months.
- Procurement: provide PO or confirm signature path; we can follow with DocuSign.
